how.title: A question is a good beginning.
how.description: We believe education comes first. Our first focus is Bitcoin: a place to ask, learn and ask again in the language you speak.
how.step1Body: Choose a language and how much detail you want. You can change either at any time. No account needed.
how.step2Title: Get an answer from reviewed knowledge.
how.step2Body: The assistant finds the knowledge your community's reviewers approved and answers from it in your language. It never asks for your seed phrase, PIN or password.
how.step3Body: On this public service, questions are answered by an outside AI service that promises not to keep them, and chats are deleted from our server after 30 days. You can delete them sooner. The AI can make mistakes.
trust.title: Trust starts with being clear.
trust.reviewBody: Nothing changes from a single chat. Members suggest better wording; it is used only after reviewers approve it. The AI does not learn from your conversations.
trust.secretsTitle: Your secrets have no place in chat.
trust.secretsBody: Afribit AI never asks for a seed phrase, private key, PIN or password. Messages containing one are refused.
trust.feedbackBody: Each assistant says where its AI runs and how long it keeps chats. Delete one chat or all of them at any time. If an answer is wrong or unsafe, report it so people can review it.
trust.openBody: Anyone can inspect and contribute to the code. Code is Apache-2.0; educational content is CC BY-SA 4.0.
safety.title: Your seed phrase is yours. Keep it that way.
safety.body: Nobody legitimate will ever ask for your seed phrase. Never type it into this chat. If someone asks for it, pause and ask for help.
safety.action: Someone asked for my seed phrase
safety.question: Someone asked for my seed phrase. Should I share it?
community.title: Your community. Your own AI.
community.description: Afribit AI is open-source software plus a community pack: your languages, your voice and your reviewed knowledge in one folder. The work is reviewing with your own people, not writing code.
community.nodeBody: A machine at your hub serves everyone on the local Wi-Fi, with your own knowledge and your own database. With its own GPU, questions never leave your network.
community.reviewTitle: Shape it in your community's words.
community.reviewBody: Anyone can suggest a better way to say an answer. Trainers and reviewers, invited by the community, approve phrases and knowledge before anyone else hears them.
faq.title: A few things to know.
faq.a1: Questions go to an outside AI service that promises not to keep or train on them. They still leave your community. Chats are deleted from our server after 30 days, and you can delete them sooner from the app. Please do not type personal details you do not need to share.
faq.a2: Yes, for learners: no payment and no account. Your mobile data charges still apply. A community can run its own node for free on its own machine. Afribit Local will be a monthly service paid by the community, never a charge per question.
faq.a3: Yes. It uses community-reviewed knowledge, but an AI-generated answer can still be wrong. You can report a wrong or unsafe answer from the chat.
faq.a4: Community reviewers check knowledge and wording before it is used. When a member suggests better wording, a reviewer approves it first, and safety topics need two reviewers. Your conversations do not train the AI.
faq.a5: No account is needed to chat or to suggest wording. Accounts are for the trainers and reviewers a community invites.
faq.a6: The public service needs internet for new answers. Once installed, the app shell opens offline and keeps your draft on this device. A community node with its own GPU answers on its local network without internet.
faq.a7: No. Afribit AI is for learning. It does not make financial decisions for you.
faq.q8: Can any community set up Afribit AI?
faq.a8: Yes. The code is open for any community to set up its own instance. Each instance has its own database and memory of reviewed knowledge, shaped by local language and priorities. A community node can host the AI locally on hardware the community manages.
faq.q9: Is Afribit AI only for Bitcoin education?
faq.a9: Education is our starting point because understanding comes first. Today’s public demo focuses on Bitcoin. The open-source engine lets communities build around their own reviewed knowledge.

node.title: Run a community node.
node.intro: Set up Afribit AI on a machine your community manages. Build around your local language, priorities and reviewed knowledge.
node.requirements: Chat on a node is free for learners. A GPU with 16 GB runs today's default model for a small group; 24 GB runs Gemma 4 26B-A4B, the open-licensed model we are moving to, subject to our tests. No GPU? Afribit Local is coming for that.
node.disclosure: Node mode keeps questions on the node. Hybrid mode can send questions to a hosted model, and the app says so. HTTPS is required to install the app. Push notifications need internet. Serving a node over the community mesh has not been tested yet.

privacy.notice:
# What happens to your questions ? plain-language notice (DRAFT)

> **Draft, updated 8 November 2026.** Community reviewers must check the English wording and prepare
> Kiswahili/Sheng versions. Legal and operational review remain pending before participant release.
> This describes the home Proxmox education staging service; other deployments need their own notice.

## The short version

- This education pilot requires a community invitation and account. Other members cannot browse
  your conversations, personal notebooks, notes or saved learning progress through the app.
- The community server operator can access stored plaintext. We have **not** implemented a
  phone-key encrypted vault, passkeys or a hardware enclave that hides your data from that operator.
- Never enter recovery words, private keys, PINs or passwords. The app checks for recognizable
  secrets and refuses detected messages; detection is not a guarantee that every secret is found.
- AI can be wrong. Check supporting material and ask a trusted educator when unsure.
  This is education, not a recommendation to invest or a service for handling your money.

## What we keep

| Information | Purpose and handling |
|---|---|
| Account email and password hash | Community sign-in. Staff manage membership and review roles. Passwords are not intentionally stored as plaintext. |
| Questions and answers | Conversation history under the deployment's configured retention setting. Server storage and browser history settings must be explained before enrollment; this draft does not promise a universal 30-day period. |
| Personal source notebooks | Text you deliberately import, plus titles and ownership records. Stored in the community-hosted source service with account/community access checks. Only import material you have permission to use. |
| Learning notes and progress | Notes you deliberately save and your place in a published chapter, scoped to your account and community. Study notes are separate from AI memory and are not automatically inserted into prompts. |
| Optional AI memory | Separately enabled personal memory can be retrieved for your questions. Each note's remote permission is separate; local-only notes must not be routed to a hosted model. |
| Operational evidence | Service, security, compute and trial records used to operate and evaluate the system. Do not assume these records are anonymous or that deleting a chat removes all logs or backups. |

We do not sell your information or automatically train model weights on your chats, sources or notes.
Importing a source is not model training. Explicit proposals to share community knowledge require a
separate review process; they do not automatically publish a private notebook or conversation.

## Where processing happens

The current private staging configuration uses the home Proxmox server and a local model. Hosted
model allowance is zero. Selected personal notebook context is locked to local model processing.
This does not mean storage is confined to your phone or unreadable to the server operator.

For a future public pilot behind Cloudflare, browser traffic crosses the internet and Cloudflare
terminates HTTPS. Cloudflare and the server operator are part of the trust boundary. Tailscale
encrypts the hop to the origin. A local model does not make this an end-to-end encrypted service.

Other deployments may offer an optional hosted provider for heavy questions. They must disclose the
provider, what is sent and the applicable policy before enabling that route. Removing names is not
a guarantee of anonymity. The current private staging service does not enable that route.

Voice input is optional. Browser/device speech services may process audio outside the community;
the app must disclose that and does not promise private or offline speech. Typing remains available.

## Your choices and limits

Delete chats using the conversation controls, remove imported notebooks/sources in My library, and
remove study notes in My space. Optional AI memory has its own controls. Ask the operator to delete
your account if no account-deletion control is available. These actions do not recall earlier answers, downloaded material
or copies already shared and approved elsewhere; reviewed contributions have separate withdrawal
handling. Contact the operator if a deletion or access request cannot be completed through the app.

**Before inviting participants**, the operator must publish actual retention periods, log handling,
backup retention and erasure procedures and verify a restore. Current evidence is an access-controlled
local database dump, not a proven encrypted backup system. We do not claim that deleted information
disappears from all backups within 14 days. These unresolved details keep this notice in draft.

## Questions or worries

Contact **eddie@afribit.africa** to ask about access, correction, deletion, an unsafe answer or privacy.
Do not include recovery words, passwords or unnecessary personal data in that message.

Maintainers: keep this notice aligned with [data stewardship](data-stewardship.md), the
[personal memory guide](../guides/personal-memory.md) and
[the pilot release gates](../guides/proxmox-education-pilot.md).
privacy.title: Where your questions go
privacy.dialogBody: This is how this assistant is set up. It is true for this server only.
privacy.location.community: This assistant runs on your community's own server. Your questions stay here.
privacy.location.afribit: Your community's data stays on its own computer. Questions are answered by Afribit's AI server in Kenya and are not stored there.
privacy.location.hybrid: Answered on your community's server. If it is down, some questions may go to an outside AI service.
privacy.location.cloud: Answered by an outside AI service that promises not to keep your question.
privacy.location.remote: Answered on another server. Ask whoever runs this assistant where it is.
privacy.location.unknown: Where your questions go depends on how this assistant is set up. See the privacy notice.
privacy.retention.none: Chats are not stored on the server; they stay on your phone.
privacy.retention.days: Chats are deleted from the server after {days} days.
privacy.retention.keep: Chats are kept on the server until you delete them.
chat.answeredOutside: Answered by an outside AI service.
history.deleteError: Could not delete it from the server. Check your connection and try again.
settings.deleteAllBody: This deletes every conversation this phone started, from the server and from this phone. It cannot be undone.
settings.deleteAllError: Some conversations could not be deleted from the server. Check your connection and try again.
feedback.shareWithReviewers: Include this question and answer so the reviewers can see them. This server does not keep chats, so otherwise they cannot.
account.deleteBody: Your account, settings and any conversations linked to it are deleted. Choose what happens to the phrases you contributed.
account.keepContributions: Keep my contributions, without my name
account.deleteError: Could not delete your account. Try again.
teach.title: Say it your way
teach.description: How would you say this answer? A community reviewer reads every suggestion. Nothing changes for anyone else until a reviewer approves it.
teach.includeQuestion: Include my question, so the reviewers understand the answer
teach.useFor: What may your suggestion be used for?
teach.useAnswers: Improving the assistant's answers, after a reviewer checks it
teach.useTraining: Training future versions of the assistant
teach.noSecrets: Never write a seed phrase, PIN, password or anyone's personal details.
teach.thanks: Thank you. A reviewer will check it. Nothing changes for anyone else until then.
teach.tooMany: Thank you! That is the most suggestions we take from one conversation for now. Try again later.
teach.error: Could not send your suggestion. Check your connection and try again.
contribute.inviteHelp: Your community's administrator gives you this code. It works once.
contribute.inviteRefused: We couldn't create the account. Check the invitation code, or ask your administrator for a new one.
contribute.inviteClosed: New accounts are not being created right now. Ask your administrator.
community.localBody: For communities without a GPU: a small box at your hub keeps your data, and Afribit's AI server in Kenya answers the questions without keeping them. A monthly service for the community; members never pay per question. We are testing it now.
faq.q10: Will it answer anything, like other AI chats?
faq.a10: Not yet. It answers from your community's approved knowledge and says when a question isn't covered. A clearly labelled "Ask anything" mode, off by default, is planned for communities that want it.
faq.a11: It depends on how each assistant is set up, and the app tells you at the top of the chat: on your community's own machine, with an outside AI service (like this public service), or, with Afribit Local, on Afribit's server in Kenya.
memory.title: Personal memory
memory.explanation: Memory is off until you enable it. Save up to 20 notes of 500 characters. Notes belong to this account and community. They are saved separately from chat retention and are never automatically used for training.
memory.historyWarning: Deleting a note does not erase earlier answers or approved shared copies. A conversation that used local-only memory stays local-only; start a new conversation for remote answers. The community host still operates this storage.
memory.localUnavailable: This setup cannot use local-only notes. Only notes you explicitly allow remotely can enter new model prompts.
memory.remote: Allow this note in prompts sent to the configured remote model service
memory.deleteAll: Delete all private notes and disable memory
memory.shareConsent: I allow reviewers to see this saved snapshot and, after two approvals, publish it for this community and its configured AI services. This does not permit training.
memory.twoReviewers: Check accuracy and permission to share. Publication requires two distinct current reviewers; submitters cannot approve their own snapshot.
memory.firstApproval: One reviewer has approved. A different reviewer is required.
memory.error: Could not complete this action. Reload to check the latest version and try again. Review permissions or memory limits may have changed.
processing.location: Where this conversation may be processed
processing.local: Keep this conversation on the community box
processing.explanation: Local-only questions never go to a remote model or embedding service. Approved-cards-only uses local text search without a model; a matching card may not answer every part of your question. The community host still controls the box.
processing.locked: This conversation stays local-only, including future history. Start a new conversation to use remote services.
processing.source.reviewed: This is the matching approved card, shown directly. No model generated this answer.
processing.source.fallback: The model could not complete this request. This is a matching approved card shown directly.
processing.source.unavailable: No answer was generated. No matching approved card was available.
processing.staysLocal: This conversation is restricted to processing on the community box.
processing.defaultNotice: This describes the service default. A conversation's Answer options can require stricter local-only processing.
